clue.text: Plot to pin crime on people already inside

indicators.note: the crime is pinned on, so it comes attached after the people

parts.note: convicts serving time are cons, people already inside prison
piracy is the crime of robbery at sea

explanation.surface: A scheme to frame prisoners for an offence they could not have committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin ... on' tells you the crime is fixed onto the end of the convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group, so it is a synonym for a plot.

clue.text: One saying nothing about one's demand

indicators.note: the silent person goes round, about, the numeral

parts.note: a clam is someone who keeps their mouth shut
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person still voices what they want.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a claim is to assert a right, so a claim is a demand.

clue.text: Philosopher reinterpreting Zen ethics

indicators.note: reinterpreting means the letters of the two words are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A thinker offers a fresh reading of Buddhist moral teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a 19th-century German philosopher, an example of the category.

clue.text: Stage and screen star, could this be?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: ARTS 'performing', that is rearranged, gives this word

explanation.surface: Asking whether a celebrated actor might embody the theatre and film world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'could this be?' invites reading the answer as an instruction: 'performing' is an anagram signal acting on ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre and film are the leading examples of the performing arts.

clue.text: Flyer produced by far-Left section of party

parts.note: a red is a far-left radical, a communist
a wing is a faction within a political party

explanation.surface: A leaflet put out by the radical faction of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The redwing is a small thrush, a bird and so a flyer.

clue.text: Pipe playing melody puts horse into easy gait

indicators.note: the letter is put into the gait

parts.note: a canter is an easy gallop, a horse's gait
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A tune being played as a rider eases a horse into a canter.
explanation.definitionFit: The chanter is the bagpipe's fingered pipe on which the tune is played.

clue.text: Scrape legs and give sharp cry

definitions.meaning: to ... your shins is to scrape the skin off them

explanation.definitionFit: Bark means both to graze the skin and to make a dog's sharp call.

clue.text: Bikini has a high price

parts.note: a toll is a heavy cost, as in 'took its toll'

explanation.surface: A swimsuit that costs a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a Pacific atoll, a ring-shaped coral island, used for nuclear tests.

clue.text: Vital committees should have computers at their fingertips here

parts.note: key means crucial, vital
boards are governing committees

explanation.surface: Important committees ought to have computing at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyboards are the parts of computers that lie under the user's fingers.

clue.text: Correct island's longitude

parts.note: right means correct
Ascension is an island in the South Atlantic

explanation.surface: Fixing the position east or west of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Right ascension is the celestial equivalent of longitude in astronomy.

clue.text: Held the Bible was not infallible?

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
erred means made a mistake, showing fallibility

explanation.surface: A sceptic maintaining that scripture contains mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert firmly, so averred means held or maintained.

clue.text: Car included in some divorce arrangement

indicators.note: the car is placed inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
a limo is a limousine, a car

explanation.surface: A vehicle forms part of a couple's divorce settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony is maintenance paid to a former spouse after a divorce.

clue.text: Singer's colour print

parts.note: a mezzo is a mezzo-soprano singer
a tint is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A vocalist's favourite colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A mezzotint is an engraving technique and the print it produces.

clue.text: Surprised cry from Inferno circle

parts.note: Dante's Inferno is hell
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A shriek of surprise from one of Dante's rings of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is used to express surprise as well as greeting.

clue.text: Not well served by this deputy?

definitions.text: Not well served by this deputy?

parts.words: Not well served by this deputy?
parts.note: a stand-in doctor serves patients who are not well; read the other way it suggests poor service

explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a stand-in doctor who covers for another, a deputy serving the sick.

clue.text: Distressed as tatty work's criticised

parts.note: tatting is a craft that makes lace, so tatting work is lace
rated in the old sense of scolded or berated

explanation.surface: Shabby handiwork earns harsh reviews, to the maker's distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tatty' suggests shabby, but here it refers to tatting, a way of making lace by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated, literally torn, is used figuratively for deeply hurt or distressed.

clue.text: Plant seed with expected result at first

parts.note: a germ is a seed or bud from which growth starts
and means together with

indicators.note: at first means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Sow a seed and get the anticipated outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb or shrub of the mint family, so a plant.

clue.text: Idle-sounding dustman

indicators.note: sounding means the answer is said like the phrase for idle

parts.note: an idle person does little

explanation.surface: A refuse collector with a reputation for laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Doolittle is the dustman father of Eliza in Shaw's Pygmalion and in My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolittle is the famous dustman character, so the definition names him by trade.

clue.text: Made a fortune from laundry business?

definitions.text: Made a fortune from laundry business?

parts.words: Made a fortune from laundry business?
parts.note: to wash and press clothes is to clean them up, and the idiom for getting rich fits the same words

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is an idiom for making a big profit, and literally describes washing.

clue.text: Devil's Disciple a failure, having gone wrong

parts.note: a dud is something that fails

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the word are put in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: A play flopped because it went off badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Dudgeon is the hero of Shaw's play The Devil's Disciple, who styles himself the devil's disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Shaw play is the man called the devil's disciple.

clue.text: Sower, for one, quietly going over farmland

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
arable land is farmland for crops

explanation.surface: A farmer sowing seed quietly crossing his fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parable of the Sower is one of Jesus's stories, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Get on wrong side of winger's pass

definitions.meaning: in football a wide player's ball into the middle

explanation.definitionFit: Cross means to annoy or oppose, and also the ball played across from the wing.

clue.text: Eccentric person of education has Latin beat

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: An odd graduate with a Latin rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance and its rhythm, a Latin American beat.

clue.text: Nothing to think about in control of computer

indicators.note: the thinking word goes about, around, the nothing

parts.note: to muse is to think
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Being in charge of a computer leaves you nothing to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a hand-held device for controlling a computer.

clue.text: Causing confusion in gardening broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast, scattered like seed, means the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio gardening show that leaves listeners baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranging means throwing into disorder, so causing confusion.

clue.text: Chap adopts English cat

indicators.note: adopts means the man takes in the letter

parts.note: gent means a man, a chap

explanation.surface: A man takes in an English cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a small spotted cat-like carnivore, loosely called a cat.

clue.text: Good chap in loyal service finally made financial overseer

indicators.note: the saint goes in the word for loyal

parts.note: true means loyal
ST, saint, is a good man

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A worthy man in faithful employment was finally put in charge of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds and manages property or money on behalf of others.

clue.text: Sound building materials given to north London community

indicators.note: Sound says the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: bricks are building materials

explanation.surface: Solid supplies sent to a district in the north of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Brixton is a district of south London; the clue's 'north' only supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Brixton is a district and community in the London borough of Lambeth.

clue.text: Stamp Act — bill dropped in parliament

parts.note: a die is a stamp for impressing coins

indicators.note: dropped means the bill is taken out of the word Act

parts.note: taken as written
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: The Stamp Act, with a bill withdrawn in the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stamp Act was a 1765 British tax on the American colonies, which only adds to the historical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet.

clue.text: Engraving captures new imposition on alien

indicators.note: captures means the burial word holds the letter

parts.note: read as en-graving, putting in a grave, it means burial

explanation.surface: A carving that contains something novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Engraving looks like etching, but split as en-grave-ing it means burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is confining enemy aliens in wartime, something imposed on them.
